new_bank_questions.title: A smooth and its intercept
new_bank_questions.body: At three observed inputs a fitted additive predictor has intercept 2 and smooth values (-1, 0, 1). Give its three fitted predictors. If the intercept is changed to 5, choose smooth values that give the same predictors. State one constraint that picks a unique intercept in this example.
new_bank_questions.answer: The fitted predictors are (1, 2, 3). Raising the intercept by 3 and lowering every smooth value by 3 gives intercept 5 and smooth values (-4, -3, -2), with the same predictors. The sum-to-zero constraint on the smooth selects the original values, whose sum is 0; the shifted smooth sums to -9.

new_bank_questions.title: Only a product is visible
new_bank_questions.body: A binary response has success probability p=ab, where 0<a<1 and 0<b<1. Compare (a,b)=(0.2,0.5) with (0.5,0.2). Are a and b separately identifiable from any number of these binary responses? Is their product identifiable?
new_bank_questions.answer: Both pairs give p=0.1, so each generates the same Bernoulli law for every response and every sample size. The individual factors a and b are not identified. The product ab is identified because distinct products give distinct Bernoulli success probabilities.
